question: A 22-year-old female presents at 24 weeks gestation with a chief complaint of burning upon urination. On physical exam, you note a gravid uterus that extends above the umbilicus. A urine analysis and culture is sent demonstrating over 100,000 colony forming units of E. coli. Of note this patient had a similar UTI 7 weeks ago that was resolved with appropriate medication. Which of the following is the most appropriate management of this patient?

options.opd: Nitrofurantoin and continue with nitrofurantoin prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy
options.ope: Cephalexin and IV antibiotic prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "22-year-old female at 24 weeks gestation" -> "presents with burning upon urination" -> "urine analysis shows >100,000 CFU of E. coli" -> "previous UTI treated 7 weeks ago" -> "consideration of safe antibiotics in pregnancy" -> "Nitrofurantoin is generally safe in pregnancy" -> "Cephalexin is also safe in pregnancy" -> "TMP-SMX is less preferred in the third trimester" -> "prophylaxis may be considered due to recurrent UTIs" -> "Nitrofurantoin and continue with nitrofurantoin prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy is appropriate" -> 85%

CHAIN: "22-year-old female at 24 weeks gestation" -> "presents with burning upon urination" -> "urine culture shows E. coli" -> "previous UTI treated 7 weeks ago" -> "risk of recurrent UTI in pregnancy" -> "antibiotic choice must consider safety in pregnancy" -> "Cephalexin is safe and effective" -> "Nitrofurantoin is also safe" -> "TMP-SMX is less ideal in late pregnancy" -> "Cephalexin and IV antibiotic prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy is a reasonable option" -> 80%

CHAIN: "22-year-old female at 24 weeks gestation" -> "presents with burning upon urination" -> "urine culture shows E. coli" -> "previous UTI treated 7 weeks ago" -> "need to treat current UTI effectively" -> "Nitrofurantoin is effective for UTI" -> "consideration of prophylaxis due to recurrent infections" -> "unclear if IV prophylaxis is necessary" -> "Nitrofurantoin and continue with nitrofurantoin prophylaxis for the rest of the pregnancy is a strong option" -> 75%
analysis: In this case, the patient is a pregnant woman with a confirmed urinary tract infection (UTI) caused by E. coli. Nitrofurantoin is generally considered safe for use in pregnancy, particularly in the second trimester, but it is not recommended for long-term prophylaxis. TMP-SMX is contraindicated in the third trimester due to the risk of kernicterus and should be avoided. Cephalexin is a safe option for treating UTIs in pregnancy and can also be used for prophylaxis. Given the patient's history of recurrent UTIs, the most appropriate management would be to treat the current infection with Cephalexin and consider prophylaxis for the remainder of the pregnancy. Therefore, the best choice is Cephalexin (option c).
